allow_large: The owner added UX items to this fix on 2026-09-27
done_when: PR titles are short (a task: story title: task name; a fix: the why's first clause, 70 characters at most), a promoted spec task's ID is SPEC, the PR body labels Why and Done when and the review block opens with a plain verdict and no hash, the board's GitHub call succeeds on this repo and links each item to its PR, and forge next says which items are ready to merge with their PR link and names the findings a close stopped on; tests through the real commands prove each; the board also lists active stories first, folds finished fixes into one collapsed line with their count, and uses plainer status words; existing tests that expect the old titles, IDs, PR body or output are updated to the new wording, since that change is deliberate

findings.body: This test checks only a clean review and excludes the old introductory phrase, not the commit hash. Always emitting the clean verdict, or putting the hash on a separate line, would still pass. The blocked-close tests in tests/test_close.py:491–494 check finding text but not the verdict. Extend the real-command coverage to assert the blocked verdict and absence of the reviewed hash in both cases.
findings.title: Not done: command-level proof of blocked verdicts and hash-free review blocks

findings.body: When configured checks pass but an additional check such as lint fails or remains pending, this path announces that the PR is ready to merge. board._green_at only examines configured names (src/forge/board.py:269–274), whereas close checks additional jobs too (src/forge/checks.py:34–50). A rejected close leaves the saved status as waiting for checks (src/forge/close.py:81–95), so this scenario reaches the new readiness path. Use the same check policy before recommending a merge.
findings.title: Apply close's check policy before announcing merge readiness

findings.body: Only the newest 25 PRs across all states now receive files and checks, but consumers still use the larger listing. The last 25 merged changes are counted in src/forge/board.py:248–257, where omitted files count as no Forge changes. Newer open or closed PRs therefore make that metric undercount. Older open PRs also lose their check-derived readiness at lines 215–223. Fetch bounded details for the relevant PRs instead of treating omitted details as negative results.
findings.title: Fetch details for the PRs whose status and metrics are displayed

findings.body: This second read uses the platform's default encoding, although review.task already reads and returns the document as UTF-8 (src/forge/review.py:85–91). On supported Windows/Python configurations without UTF-8 mode, non-ASCII story content can corrupt the title or raise UnicodeDecodeError, stopping close before PR creation. Use the returned text or specify encoding="utf-8".
findings.title: Reuse the UTF-8 story text when extracting the title

why: Forge's pull requests and status output bury what the owner must do: titles run to 300 characters, promoted spec tasks get 40-character IDs, PR bodies and review blocks carry hashes and jargon, the board times out on GitHub and has no links, and forge next never says what is ready to merge or why a close stopped
